description:
SheOrbit is a team of enthusiastic students passionate about space science, technology, innovation, and problem-solving. As part of NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to explore real-world challenges using NASA Earth observation data. Through creativity, collaboration, and coding, we hope to develop innovative solutions for sustainable agriculture and a better future.

Together, we dream, code, and explore!
summary:
AgroOrbit is a smart crop rotation decision-support platform designed to help farmers make informed and sustainable farming decisions using NASA Earth observation data. The platform provides a farmer-friendly dashboard where users can enter their location, soil type, previous crop, and farm area to receive suitable crop rotation suggestions.

AgroOrbit integrates NASA POWER data to display location-based weather and climate information, including temperature, precipitation, humidity, and solar radiation. It also provides access to NASA resources such as GPM IMERG rainfall data and SMAP soil moisture information for further exploration.

By combining farm details, crop rotation suggestions, and Earth observation resources in one platform, AgroOrbit aims to support better agricultural planning, encourage sustainable farming practices, and improve awareness of environmental conditions. Our goal is to make satellite-based information more accessible and useful for farmers.
details:
AgroOrbit – Grow Smarter. Farm Better.

AgroOrbit is a smart crop rotation decision-support platform designed to help farmers make informed and sustainable farming decisions using Earth observation data.

The platform allows farmers to enter their country, state, district, soil type, previous crop, and farm area. Based on these details, it provides suitable crop rotation suggestions through a rule-based recommendation system.

AgroOrbit integrates NASA POWER data to display location-based weather and climate information, including temperature, precipitation, humidity, and solar radiation. It also provides links to NASA GPM IMERG rainfall data and SMAP soil moisture resources for further exploration.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with API integration for location selection and environmental data.

AgroOrbit aims to make satellite-based information easier to understand and accessible to farmers, encourage sustainable agricultural practices, and support better crop planning.

Our creative approach combines farmer inputs, crop rotation suggestions, and NASA Earth observation resources in one user-friendly platform. It is a prototype, and crop recommendations should be verified with local agricultural experts.
